purpose: consolidated result of the dataset-map build; consult BEFORE asserting anything about these layers, and read the verification column before treating a row as established
fast_test: layer-linked (perturbation, gene) pairs vs pairs matched on perturbation-strength x gene-responsiveness deciles, Replogle K562, |robust z|. Raw held-out ratios, never a difference from a shuffle. Reference: PPI 1.208x, co-dependency 1.070x, regulatory 1.021x, signalling 1.028x (null). Below ~1.05 is not interesting.

verification_meaning.reviewed: an adversarial agent was tasked with refuting the reported effect and the module was revised as a result
verification_meaning.single-pass: built and self-tested against the project's controls, but no independent attempt was made to break it. Weaker evidence than a reviewed row, and the workflows were stopped early to conserve usage rather than because these were finished

items.question: does the perturbational layer's sign survive a change of cell line?
items.verdict: THE INCREMENT SURVIVES THE HARD MOVE. All 4 cell lines that leave Replogle's laboratory keep a positive, edge-specific sign increment significant on 100% of 25 matched draws (magnitude ratio 1.15x-1.45x). It decays with distance from the source -- Jurkat +21.9, HepG2 +18.5, HCT116 +10.8, melanoma +5.5 points against the RPE1 baseline's +15.0 -- but it never reaches zero and it never inverts. RPE1 was NOT flattered by being the same lab: Jurkat and HepG2 exceed it, so on the lineage axis RPE1 was if anything the harder test, and the ordering that does appear tracks assay and library distance rather than laboratory -- CRISPRi lines that share Replogle's library sit highest, the independent genome-wide CRISPRi screen sits in the middle, and the Cas9-knockout melanoma panel, which changes the perturbation modality itself, sits lowest at +5.5. Restricting HCT116 to the 1,906 perturbations it shares with Replogle's essential library lifts its increment from +10.8 to +13.5 points, so part of the decay down the ladder is which perturbations are shared rather than how far the cell line has moved. No line shows agreement significantly below its swapped-source control, so where the increment is absent it is NOT DETECTED, not reversed. The harness reproduces the published RPE1 baseline it is testing against (1.306x and +15.0 points against 1.309x and +15.0), so the comparison is between cell lines and not between implementations.
limits: the layer is NOT rebuilt here -- the same K562 edge set is re-tested, so a defect in the source edge definition propagates to every row of the table unchanged

each cell line uses ONE pipeline internally, but the pipelines differ BETWEEN lines: the four scPerturb/Replogle lines are log2(1+CPM of summed counts) minus control, HCT116 is Xaira's mean log1p(CP10k) minus non-targeting. Per-gene robust z is affine-invariant so this does not distort a within-line comparison, but raw |z| is NOT comparable across rows of the table and only the within-line ratios are
Frangieh and Shifrut are Cas9 KNOCKOUT while the source is CRISPRi KNOCKDOWN; a missing effect there can be modality rather than lineage, and this design cannot separate the two
Jurkat and HepG2 use the same Replogle essential-gene library as the source, so they change the lab and the lineage but not the perturbation set -- they are an intermediate rung, not the hardest one
Shifrut (20 targets) and Papalexi (25 targets) are excluded on a bar fixed before any measurement; they are UNTESTED, not negative

only genes measured in BOTH cell lines are testable, and coverage differs sharply (8,248 K562 genes against 23,712 Frangieh features); an edge to a gene not measured in the target line is unknown, never absent
genes with zero MAD in a target line have no definable z and are dropped rather than zeroed; the count is reported per line

the HCT116 matrix arrives pre-assembled by fetch_xaira.py at its own >= 20 cells/perturbation threshold, not this module's >= 25, and its per-perturbation cell counts are not carried in the file -- so that row is slightly more permissive about noisy perturbations than the rest

the source-swap null holds the target gene fixed and matches only on perturbation-strength decile, so a residual confound correlated with strength within a decile would inflate the increment; the residual SMD is reported but is not proof of no confounding
K562 perturbation symbols collapse 11,258 transcript-level rows onto 9,867 genes and the last row per symbol wins, exactly as in causal_reg.py -- consistent with the baseline but arbitrary

self-edges (the perturbed gene read on itself) are a near-guaranteed agreement in both lines because the perturbation depletes its own transcript (CRISPRi directly, Cas9 via nonsense-mediated decay); they are 0.5-1.5% of edges and the increment with them removed is reported per line, but the headline figure keeps them so that it replicates causal_reg.py exactly
no correction for multiple cell lines; the reported per-line significance is within-line

items.question: rebuild PPI retaining cell line and confidence
items.verdict: THIS LAYER CARRIES A REAL BUT SMALL SIGNAL THAT DOES NOT CLEAR THE PRESPECIFIED 1.05x THRESHOLD ONCE THE CONTROL IS PROPERLY MATCHED. BioPlex 3.0 yields 188,164 directed AP-MS edges (117,569 in 293T, 70,595 in HCT116) over 166,351 distinct gene pairs; 95.0% of endpoints join by UniProt accession and only 59 by symbol (99.4% carry an id by some route). Only 61.4% of the in-cell BioPlex pairs are already in the existing 191,447-tuple PPI layer, so this is a rebuild that also adds 52,140 pairs that layer does not have. EFFECT SIZE: mean |robust z| of the 139,034 linked (perturbation, gene) pairs is 1.1061, over 74,368 distinct gene pairs from 8,119 perturbed genes. The CONTRAST depends on how tight the control is, and that is the correction this version makes: at the project's legacy decile matching the ratio is 1.102x, but that control leaves the linked rows 1.1% stronger and the linked columns 0.7% more responsive on the MEAN while its rank test passes at p 0.32. Tightening the bins moves the ratio monotonically to 1.068x, where the residual mean ratio reaches 0.9984/0.9997 and stops moving (1.069x at 320x320). Holding the perturbation EXACTLY -- drawing the control gene from the same knockdown, matched on responsiveness -- gives 1.034x (100% of 20 draws p<0.05; cluster-robust 95% CI over perturbed genes [1.024, 1.044]). The sham arm returns 1.004x at that tightness, so the tightened instrument is not manufacturing a deflation. Ranking is only meaningful at a fixed control tightness, so the two layers this one is usually compared against were re-measured here with the same instrument. At the legacy decile rung: existing PPI 1.173x, BioPlex 1.102x, co-dependency 1.068x -- which is where the earlier 'BioPlex sits between them' reading came from. At the exact-perturbation control the order changes: existing PPI 1.058x, co-dependency 1.053x, BioPlex 1.034x. BioPlex is the WEAKEST of the three once perturbation-level confounding is removed by construction rather than approximated with bins. Confidence was NOT worth keeping for this purpose: matched head-to-head at 40x40, top-tercile pInt reaches 1.0606 against 1.0588 for the bottom tercile (1.002x, median p 0.76, 0% of draws p<0.05). Above the 0.75 publication floor pInt does not resolve which edges couple transcriptionally in K562; it is stored, not weighted. At the legacy rung this arm read 0.984x, i.e. the 'wrong' way -- that was a composition artefact of the coarse match, not a reversal. Cross-cell-line reproducibility is the one metadata field that does anything, but less than the earlier reading claimed: both-lines vs one-line, matched on strength x responsiveness x BioPlex degree, is 1.034x (median p 0.0074, 90% of draws) at 40x40, down from 1.043x at the legacy rung. It is also not separable from prior knowledge: adding 'already in the existing PPI layer' as a fourth axis leaves 1.016x at 0% of draws on n=5,755, which is underpowered for an effect of that size and so neither confirms nor refutes it. The honest statement is that 'seen in two lines' is worth about as much as the whole layer is. The pairs BioPlex adds that the existing layer lacks are not noise but they are weak: 1.029x against the exact-perturbation control on 60,690 pairs (90% of draws p<0.05), against 1.041x for the pairs that were already known. Bait/prey direction buys nothing on this readout (1.005x matched, median p 0.71, 0% of draws), so it is stored for provenance and not used as a weight. Coverage is biased on both matched covariates (5,499/9,864 perturbed genes are baits, strength p 0.13; 7,276/8,248 measured genes appear in BioPlex, responsiveness p 2.2e-16) and the linked pairs are also enriched for well-studied, abundant, high-degree genes on every one of publication count, ppm, gene length and both degree measures -- none of which individually accounts for the effect, but all of which the layer inherits. A missing edge is stored as unknown, never as zero.
limits: THE HEADLINE DEPENDS ON HOW TIGHTLY THE CONTROL IS MATCHED, so a single ratio is not quotable without its rung. Decile matching gives 1.102x but leaves the linked rows 1.1% stronger and the linked columns 0.7% more responsive than their controls ON THE MEAN, which is what the ratio is a ratio of; a Mann-Whitney rank test does not detect this and passed it. The converged joint control gives 1.068x and the exact-perturbation control 1.034x.

RATIOS FROM DIFFERENT MODULES ARE NOT COMPARABLE unless they were computed at the same control tightness. That is why the existing PPI and co-dependency layers are re-measured here rather than quoted; their published decile-rung numbers are inflated by the same mechanism.

NEITHER CELL LINE IS K562. BioPlex 3.0 is HEK293T and HCT116; the fast test asks whether an interaction found in those lines constrains the K562 transcriptional response, which is a transfer question, not a within-cell measurement. Nothing here establishes that any given edge exists in K562.
AP-MS reports CO-COMPLEX MEMBERSHIP, not binary direct contact. A bait->prey edge may be bridged by one or more other proteins; the direction is experimental (who was tagged), not mechanistic.

The released network is already filtered at pInt >= 0.75, so the 'low confidence' arm is 0.75-tercile, not a genuine low-confidence tail. The confidence test therefore measures resolution WITHIN the published set and says nothing about edges BioPlex rejected.

Bait selection is not random and neither is prey detectability: baits skew to well-expressed, clonable ORFs and prey to abundant proteins. Absence of an edge among non-baits is UNKNOWN, never evidence of no interaction.

Publication count, protein abundance, gene length, BioPlex degree and existing-PPI degree are all significantly imbalanced between linked pairs and the decile-matched control (table above). Each was added as a third matching axis and none of them individually accounts for the effect, but the layer is measurably concentrated on well-studied, abundant, highly connected genes and any downstream use inherits that.
Overexpression of a tagged bait can create interactions that do not occur at endogenous stoichiometry; BioPlex mitigates this with near-endogenous promoters but does not eliminate it.

The GWPS readout is transcriptional. A physical interaction that acts post-translationally leaves no signature in this test, so a null here is a null for TRANSCRIPTIONAL coupling only -- it is not evidence against the interaction.

Endpoints are joined to the registry by UniProt accession first (95.0% of endpoints); 577 resolve only by Entrez and 59 only by gene symbol, recorded via=symbol, the weakest key. 85 endpoints carry no entity id at all.
The registry's gene|entrez alias keys are stored as floats ('7105.0'); this module normalises on its side. Any layer joining raw integer Entrez ids against this registry will silently match nothing.
pW/pNI/pInt come from one CompPASS-plus model fitted to this release. They are not comparable to STRING confidences, MIscores, or the confidences of any other release, and must not be pooled.

788 genes are perturbed by more than one construct, and far more importantly one perturbation contributes hundreds of linked columns, so the 139,034 pairs are not 139,034 independent observations. Mann-Whitney p-values are optimistic by construction; the cluster-robust interval over 8,119 perturbed genes is the honest one.

The cell-line result is not separable from prior knowledge at the available power: matching additionally on whether the pair is already in the existing PPI layer drops the both-vs-one contrast to a null on a fifth of the data, which is underpowered for an effect of that size and therefore neither confirms nor refutes it.

Every ratio here is a contrast against a matched control drawn from the SAME perturbation matrix; no arm has been validated on a held-out cell line, so this measures association within K562 Perturb-seq, not predictive transfer.

items.question: protein complexes with citable provenance
items.verdict: CO-COMPLEX MEMBERSHIP CARRIES REAL SIGNAL, BUT ONLY FOR LARGE MACHINES. CORUM 5.3 contributes 5,315 human complexes over 48,377 distinct co-complex gene pairs, which resolve to 86,364 testable (perturbation, gene) cells in GWPS -- 3.1x the testable surface of the 2,039 complexes already in the cell object, which share only 11,282 of those gene pairs with CORUM and not one complex NAME. Matched over 20 draws, co-complex pairs reach a RAW mean |z| of 1.4629 against 1.2066 matched -- a ratio of 1.212 over 86,364 pairs, median p 0, 100% of draws p<0.05. That is the strongest link type this test has scored, level with PPI (1.208x) and well above co-dependency (1.070x) and regulatory (1.021x). Decile matching leaves a residual imbalance on gene responsiveness (p 3e-06), so the test was re-run at 50x50 bins where that clears (p 0.47); the ratio softens to 1.165 and stays significant in 100% of draws, so the effect is not the covariate talking. The signal is entirely in the big complexes: >5 subunits gives 1.230 over 76,243 pairs (100% of draws p<0.05) while <=5 subunits gives 1.054 over 10,121 pairs and reaches p<0.05 in 0% of them. That is not a power artefact: subsampled to the small set's exact n of 10,121, large complexes still score 1.230 at median p 4.47e-18 in 100% of draws. Across bands the effect is a GRADIENT rather than a threshold: 2 (heterodimer) 1.063, 3-5 1.051, 6-10 1.047, 11-20 1.182, >20 1.259. The practical consequence is that a CORUM heterodimer edge should not be admitted on the strength of the pooled number -- the pooled number is the ribosome and the spliceosome. CORUM IS BROADER, NOT BETTER PER PAIR: on the identical test the existing untraceable layer scores 1.251 over its 27,609 cells, slightly ABOVE CORUM's 1.212 -- what CORUM buys is 3.1x the coverage and a citable provenance, not a stronger edge, so the two should be unioned rather than one swapped for the other. And the ASSUMED 1:1:1 limiting-subunit capacity earns nothing: the lowest-abundance subunit is LESS disruptive to knock down than its complex-mates (-0.0944, Wilcoxon p 1.72e-12, 38% positive over 833 complexes), so the assumption is recorded as falsified rather than carried.
limits: CORUM 5.3 is a LITERATURE-CURATED set, so it inherits publication bias: the complexes with many subunits are the ones many groups have worked on, and the size effect below is therefore confounded with how well studied a machine is. Nothing here separates those two.
most CORUM complexes were characterised in HEK293, HeLa or in vitro, NOT in K562 -- membership is imported from a different cellular context than the Perturb-seq matrix it is tested against
no stoichiometry: 5,576/5,628 complexes carry an empty subunits_stoechiometrie column. Any limiting-subunit capacity in this layer is ASSUMED 1:1:1 and is labelled ASSUMED_1_1_1

the capacity is computed only where EVERY subunit has a K562 protein measurement (a minimum over a partially measured complex is not a minimum); the rest carry null, and K562 protein coverage is itself abundance-biased, so those nulls are not missing at random
a co-complex pair here is UNDIRECTED and UNSIGNED: the test measures |z| only, so it says nothing about whether losing a subunit raises or lowers its partners

the pairs tested are only those where one member is perturbed and the other measured in GWPS; 48,377 curated pairs collapse to 86,364 testable cells, and the survivors are biased toward well-expressed genes
complexes are treated as flat membership sets -- CORUM's own hierarchy (a complex that is a module of a larger one) is discarded, so the size bands mix modules with the machines that contain them
the existing 2,039-complex layer is compared, not replaced, and its provenance remains UNKNOWN; this module cannot say which of the two is right where they disagree

items.question: does compartment gating improve the PPI layer?
items.verdict: The ungated PPI layer reproduces its reference figure (1.177x against 1.208x on 213,269 testable pairs), so this is the same pipeline the other layers were scored with. GATING ON SHARED COMPARTMENT IS A NULL AS USUALLY STATED, AND WHAT SURVIVES IS NOT `COMPARTMENT` BUT 3 PARTICULAR COMPARTMENTS. Matched head to head on perturbation strength and gene responsiveness over 20 draws of 59,443 pairs each, co-localized PPI edges reach mean |z| 1.2425 against 1.2406 for non-co-localized (1.001x, median p 0.00762, 85% of draws p<0.05). Unmatched, the co-localized arm looks clearly better (1.344 vs 1.241 raw mean |z|, 1.183x vs 1.158x against their own non-linked controls); essentially all of that gap is perturbation strength and gene responsiveness, and it disappears when those are matched. The null has a specific cause: nucleoplasm and cytosol alone account for 71% of all shared-location events, so `co-localized` mostly means `both are nuclear or both are cytosolic`, which the gene-responsiveness covariate already encodes -- sharing ONLY a hub scores 0.979x (0% of draws p<0.05). Requiring the shared location to be outside those hubs does separate (1.5076 vs 1.4332, 1.052x, median p 1.28e-10, 100% of draws, n=26,678), and it survives the adversarial round: 1.047x with locations-per-pair matched exactly, 1.082x against hub-co-localized pairs rather than against nothing, 1.063x on Enhanced|Supported annotations only, 1.024x at 50x50 bins. BUT THE PER-COMPARTMENT BREAKDOWN IS WHERE THE HONEST ANSWER IS, and it is not uniform: the whole effect sits in Endoplasmic reticulum 1.131x, Nucleoli 1.117x, Mitochondria 1.033x, while Vesicles 0.923x, Nuclear speckles 0.951x, Plasma membrane 0.951x, Golgi apparatus 0.978x are at or below 1.0. Those winners are the compartments with dedicated, transcriptionally co-regulated biogenesis programs (ribosome biogenesis, mitochondrial import and OXPHOS, the secretory/UPR machinery); the losers are traffic destinations, where two proteins can share an address without sharing a regulatory program. So the usable rule is not `gate PPI on shared compartment` -- that buys 0.999x, nothing -- but `co-residence in Endoplasmic reticulum, Nucleoli or similar biogenesis compartments is worth 13% at best`, which is around co-dependency (1.070x) and well below PPI itself (1.208x). Separately from the gating result, the layer fixes a real data-structure error: HPA gives 61% of the 13,599 annotated genes MORE THAN ONE location (mean 2.04, 8,325 genes), which the one-word `comp` field structurally cannot hold, and where both vocabularies can speak `comp` is inside the HPA set for 75% of 9,411 genes against a 29% label-shuffled baseline. Absence of an HPA call is kept as UNKNOWN and run as its own arm (1.180x -- indistinguishable from the annotated arms, so the missingness does not bias the split), never folded into the negative class.
limits: immunofluorescence with one antibody per gene in a small panel of cell lines (mostly U-2 OS, A-431, U-251MG) -- NOT K562, so a location here is not a measurement of the cell being modelled and compartment can be cell-type dependent
antibody-based: an unvalidated antibody gives a wrong location, which is why Reliability is carried per gene and 792 Uncertain calls are kept but flagged rather than deleted

31% of cell genes have no HPA annotation, and the hole is not random (annotated genes have higher dep_frac and higher PPI degree, both p<1e-10) -- absence is stored as UNKNOWN and run as its own arm, never as `not co-localized`
co-localization here is annotation overlap, not contact: two proteins in the nucleoplasm may never touch, and the shared-compartment test cannot distinguish that from a real interface

the 12-word `comp` vocabulary contains two words (membrane, extracellular) that HPA's IF vocabulary cannot express at all, so the agreement figure is computed on the remainder and says nothing about those genes

HPA's `Vesicles` term pools endosomes, lysosomes, peroxisomes, lipid droplets and secretory vesicles; it is left unmapped rather than forced into one of the 12, so 2,488 genes are outside the agreement figure
steady-state localization of an unperturbed cell: it says nothing about relocalization after a perturbation, which is what a dynamic model would need
the gating test measures whether shared compartment enriches for transcriptionally coupled PPI edges; it does NOT establish that non-co-localized edges are false

`co-localized` is dominated by two terms -- nucleoplasm and cytosol account for most shared-location events -- so the pooled gating number is close to a nuclear/cytosolic indicator, which the gene-responsiveness covariate already partly encodes; the hub/non-hub split is what separates the two and it was prespecified, not chosen after seeing the pooled result

the per-compartment breakdown is EXPLORATORY, not prespecified: it was run after the non-hub arm came back positive. Seven compartments were tested against one pool with no multiplicity correction, so the individual ratios are hypothesis-generating and the three positive ones need an independent replication before they are used as a gate

the readout is transcriptional response in K562 CRISPRi. An interaction can be real, compartment-consistent and produce no transcriptional consequence, so this test bounds the DECISION VALUE of compartment gating for this readout only -- it is not a test of whether the interactions are physically real

items.question: positioned PTM sites and modifying enzymes
items.verdict: BOTH TESTS ARE NULL, AND TEST A IS NULL WITH REAL POWER BEHIND IT: AN ANNOTATED PTM SITE SAYS NOTHING ABOUT HOW A TRANSCRIPT MOVES IN THIS CELL. Test A: genes with >= 5 annotated phosphosites (1,734 of 7,043 testable) reach raw mean |lfc| 0.07883 against 0.07863 for zero-site genes matched on publication-count and protein-length deciles over 20 draws -- a ratio of 1.0025 on a design that would have caught 1.0170 at 80% power, and it falls to 0.9922 once K562 mRNA abundance is matched too. Several of those rows do reach p<0.05 in most draws; at a ratio of 1.002 that is a shape difference, not an effect, and reporting it as one would be this project's recurring error. The partial Spearman of site count against responsiveness, controlling log pubs, log length and log mRNA, is -0.0041. Test B: 2,810 testable (P,G) cells from 5,136 iPTMnet enzyme->substrate gene pairs give raw mean |z| 0.8899 against 0.8969 matched on perturbation-strength x gene-responsiveness deciles -- 0.9924x. The arm where a transcriptional effect is actually predicted, enzyme -> TF-substrate, gives 0.9713x on 776 pairs; the direction control, perturbing the SUBSTRATE and reading the ENZYME's transcript, gives 1.0414x, i.e. if anything the edges run backwards in this assay, which is what a set of edges with no transcriptional content looks like. WHAT TEST B CAN AND CANNOT EXCLUDE, stated rather than implied. Only 2,810 (P,G) cells are testable against PPI's 94,368, so its p-values are weak evidence and its interval is the real answer: the ratio's bootstrap 95% CI is [0.943, 1.042], which excludes a PPI-sized (1.208x) or CORUM-sized effect but does NOT exclude a co-dependency-sized 1.07x one. The power control makes that concrete: BioPlex 3.0 through this identical machinery scores 1.088x on 75,639 pairs, and subsampled to exactly 2,810 pairs it still returns the same point estimate (1.089x) but reaches p<0.05 in only 20% of draws -- so at this n the design recovers a real effect's SIZE and loses its SIGNIFICANCE, and a null p here would have proved nothing on its own. The sham arm, random pairs redrawn every draw at the same n, sits at 0.996x [0.942, 1.049] as it must. THE HONEST READING IS NOT THAT THE 74,862 POSITIONED SITES OR THE 5,136 ENZYME EDGES ARE WRONG. Site existence is a property of the protein and of the literature -- rho 0.44 with publication count and 0.46 with protein length -- and phosphorylation is post-translational, so a transcriptional readout is close to blind to it by construction. The layer earns its place on capability, not on this score: positions, residues, evidence codes and named enzymes are what an activity model needs, and the field it replaces (8,425 bare counts with no site and no enzyme) could not support a single one of those questions. But it must not be wired into a transcript-level predictor as a feature, and site count must never be used as a proxy for pathway activity. What would overturn this is a K562 phosphoproteome measured after perturbation -- the occupancy this layer explicitly does not have; nothing here substitutes for one.
limits: A SITE ANNOTATION IS NOT AN OCCUPIED SITE. UniProt MOD_RES says the residue is modified somewhere in some experiment; 15,980 of 74,862 sites carry ECO:0000250 (by similarity, usually from a mouse ortholog) and 32,090 carry ECO:0007744 (proteome-wide MS, mostly not K562), against only 14,489 with direct manual experimental evidence. Nothing here measures phosphorylation IN K562, so no site can be called active, and site count must never be read as pathway activity.

SITE COUNT IS PARTLY A MEASURE OF STUDY EFFORT. rho 0.44 with publication count and 0.46 with protein length. Every gene-level number here is matched on both; the unmatched correlation is meaningless and is not reported as a result.

PERTURB-SEQ IS A TRANSCRIPTIONAL READOUT AND PTM IS POST-TRANSLATIONAL. A null in Test B is consistent with the edges being correct and the assay being blind to them. This module cannot distinguish 'these edges are wrong' from 'mRNA does not see them'; that would take a K562 phosphoproteome after perturbation, which does not exist at this scale.

ENZYME COVERAGE IS THIN AND BIASED. 5,136 enzyme->substrate gene pairs from 386 enzymes, of which only 261 are also Perturb-seq perturbations -- kinases studied since the 1990s. hprd (2009) and SIGNOR contribute most enzyme rows, so the edge set reflects two decades of kinase literature, not a survey.

THE UNIPROT 'by X' LABELS ARE MOSTLY NOT GENES. 629 free-text strings covering 4,363 annotations; only 1,990 of those annotations use a string that is itself a gene symbol. The commonest (PKA, CK2, PKC, GSK3-beta, AMPK) name FAMILIES with several catalytic subunit genes, and 639 say only 'autocatalysis'. They are stored as text and are resolved into edges only where the string is itself a symbol, recorded via=symbol.

ABSENCE IS UNKNOWN. A gene with no reviewed UniProt entry is excluded, not scored as zero sites; a reviewed protein with no MOD_RES is scored as zero ANNOTATED sites, which is a statement about UniProt, not about the protein. Missingness is biased toward the unpublished and the short.

ISOFORMS ARE COLLAPSED. Positions are on the canonical UniProt sequence; iPTMnet isoform accessions are truncated to the canonical accession, so a site position is only valid against the canonical sequence of that release.

ONE RELEASE EACH, AND THE RESULTS ARE NOT PORTABLE ACROSS RELEASES. UniProt 2026_02 and iPTMnet 6.2 are asserted at runtime; site counts grow every release, so the HIGH/LOW cut at 5 sites is release-specific.
TEST A IS A GENE-LEVEL RATIO AND IS NOT COMPARABLE TO THE PAIR-LEVEL REFERENCE NUMBERS (PPI 1.208x etc.). Only Test B is.

TEST B IS UNDERPOWERED FOR SMALL EFFECTS AND ITS p-VALUES ARE NOT THE EVIDENCE. 2,810 testable pairs against PPI's 94,368. The bootstrap 95% CI on the ratio is [0.943, 1.042]: a PPI- or CORUM-sized effect (1.21x) is excluded, a co-dependency-sized one (1.07x) is not. The BioPlex-at-the-same-n control returns the correct point estimate and loses significance, which is why effect sizes and intervals are reported here rather than p-values.

TEST A's MATCHED DRAWS OVERLAP. Only ~800 genes per arm survive matching out of pools of 1,734 and 2,672, so the 20 draws share most of their members and the fraction of draws reaching p<0.05 is not 20 independent tests. It is reported as a stability check on the draw, not as replication.

items.question: codependency scored on the RIGHT endpoint (viability, not RNA)
items.verdict: THIS LAYER CARRIES VIABILITY INFORMATION AND ALMOST NO TRANSCRIPTIONAL INFORMATION, and the two were previously graded with one number. Held out by construction -- built on half the 1,150 DepMap 24Q2 lines, scored on the other half -- co-dependent pairs reach a raw mean dependency-profile correlation of 0.1817 on lines the build never saw, against 0.0034 for pairs matched on mean dependency, dependency spread and expression (AUC 0.926, 100% of 100 draws p<0.05 over 5 independent splits; residual imbalance p 0.15/0.0021/0.08). It survives all three falsification checks: hubness as a fourth matched covariate leaves 0.1817 vs 0.0045 (AUC 0.908); centring every held-out profile within its Oncotree lineage, which deletes all between-lineage structure, leaves 0.1707 vs 0.0047 (AUC 0.914); and projecting the 5 strongest global axes -- growth rate, screen quality, broad essentiality -- out of the held-out half leaves 0.0902 vs 0.0025 (AUC 0.757). So it is not hub, lineage or global-axis bookkeeping. It is NOT uniform across edge types: pairs of common essentials reach 0.2570 (AUC 0.961) against 0.1761 (AUC 0.924) for pairs with neither -- and the project's own dataset plan has this backwards, recording pan-essentials as a structural blind spot when in this release they carry LARGER dependency spread (0.283 vs 0.127) and MORE partners (96% vs 84%). On the transcriptional fast test the SAME pairs give 1.068x (56,403 testable cells, median p 7.99e-09, AUC 0.510) -- just over the 1.05 floor, against PPI's 1.208x -- and it barely moves with co-dependency strength (whole range 0.027 across bands) (ratios 1.059, 1.070, 1.087, 1.077 across r bands 0.20/0.25/0.30/0.40+), so the two endpoints are close to orthogonal rather than one being a weak version of the other. An AUC of 0.510 is the number to keep: the transcriptional effect is real (median p 7.99e-09, 100% of draws) and useless for deciding anything about a single pair. What little of it there is looks like shared essentiality rather than partnership -- at 30x30 bins, common-essential pairs give 1.105x against 1.043x for pairs with neither. Provenance for the pre-existing layer is recovered rather than assumed: my correlations agree with its stated values at r=0.983 and recover 70% of its pairs, so it is DepMap gene-effect Pearson from a nearby release. The `sl` layer is co-dependency mislabelled -- all 1,256 pairs are POSITIVELY correlated, which is co-requirement, the opposite sign of evidence from synthetic lethality.
limits: one release (DepMap 24Q2 Public); co-dependency values shift between releases as lines are added -- the existing layer agrees at r=0.983 but is not identical, and mixing them would mix line sets
Pearson correlation across a cancer cell line panel is not a mechanism: it cannot separate same-complex, same-pathway, shared-lineage-requirement and shared-screen-artefact
the panel is CANCER cell lines grown in 2D; a co-dependency that exists only in that context will not be marked as such here
1,336 genes dropped for incomplete profiles and the drop is not random (mean gene effect -0.1884 against -0.1432 for kept genes, MWU p 7.2e-29), so absence from this layer is unknown, not zero
expression is unknown for 9 genes; those pairs are excluded from the matched arm rather than zero-filled
the layer is SYMMETRIC and unsigned as to direction: it says A and B are needed together, not that A acts on B or that either is upstream

PAN-ESSENTIALS ARE OVER-CONNECTED, NOT INVISIBLE. The project's dataset plan says this layer is structurally blind to them; in DepMap 24Q2 Public they have LARGER dependency spread (0.283 vs 0.127) and MORE partners (96% vs 84%). Their spread is largely a shared growth-rate / screen-quality axis, so a common-essential pair is the edge type most likely to be non-specific -- see the common-essential split and the global-axis-removed arm before trusting one
it is NOT synthetic lethality. Positive co-dependency is co-requirement; SL is the opposite sign of evidence and is not measurable from this file

the transcriptional numbers in this module are a measurement of a DIFFERENT endpoint, not a grade of this layer -- and they are also a different CONTEXT: one cell line (K562) against a 1,150-line panel, so 'orthogonal endpoints' and 'orthogonal contexts' are not separated here
CRISPR gene effect is Chronos-corrected; copy number and screen-quality corrections are the pipeline's, and are inherited rather than validated here

the half-splits are held out at the level of CELL LINES, not of the whole pipeline: Chronos was fitted across all 1,150 lines before this module saw the matrix, so a shared correction could leak a little structure between halves. The held-out number is an upper bound to that extent, and the lineage-centred arm is the check that bounds it from the other side

items.question: is cell-matched K562 RNA a better covariate than generic abundance?
items.verdict: CELL-MATCHED RNA IS THE BETTER COVARIATE, ON BOTH AXES AND BY A MARGIN THAT SURVIVES RESAMPLING. Against gene responsiveness it reaches Spearman +0.329 where the generic `ppm` reaches +0.268 on the same 6,976 genes (K562 wins 100% of 2,000 gene bootstraps, delta|rho| +0.061 [+0.039, +0.084]); against perturbation strength +0.173 against +0.130 over 8,620 perturbed genes (100% of bootstraps). In raw held-out terms the top decile of K562 expression carries mean |z| 1.095 against 0.831 in the bottom (1.317x) where the generic table separates only 1.211x. The mechanism behind the second axis holds: perturbations of the 830 targets SILENT in K562 (TPM < 1.0) reach mean |z| 0.824 against 0.918 for expressed targets (p 5.2e-09) -- at or below the 0.859 floor set by 585 non-targeting guides, i.e. inert, which is what CRISPRi at an already-silent promoter should look like. HOW MUCH OF THAT IS NEW is a separate question and the answer is: not much that is demonstrable. Inside generic-abundance deciles the same contrast shrinks from 1.114x to 1.040x (0.857 vs 0.824) and reaches p<0.05 in only 35% of 20 draws of ~830 per arm, so most of what K562 expression knows about inert perturbations the generic table already knew, and the residual is not established at this n. WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY, WHICH IS THE PART THAT DECIDES WHETHER TO CARRY IT: the swap does not change a banked number. Re-matching the existing PPI layer's fast test with a third axis of measured-gene abundance moves the ratio from 1.1761 (two axes, 212,924 pairs) to 1.1720 with the generic table and 1.1697 with K562 RNA. Paired over 40 seeds -- the only way a difference smaller than either arm's draw-to-draw range is readable at all -- the K562 covariate absorbs more (-0.00236, signed-rank p 0.00019, more in 78% of individual draws), so the generic table was under-controlling in the predicted direction. The size of that under-control is 3.7% of PPI's 17.6% excess. That is real but small: PPI's ratio is not an abundance artefact under either covariate, and swapping them would not have changed a single admission decision this project has made. The better covariate is established; its consequence for this particular layer is not. Promoter accessibility adds nothing on top of the expression level: matched on K562 TPM decile, promoters open in all 4 ATAC experiments carry mean |z| 0.8962 against 0.9050 for promoters open in none (0.9904x over 20 draws) -- a ratio BELOW 1, i.e. if anything the accessible promoters are marginally less responsive, and the unmatched Spearman is -0.074. Accessibility is kept in the layer as state, not as a predictor. Finally, the prescribed pair fast test behaves exactly as predicted before it was run: 1.010x on 131,348 expression-defined pairs, because matching on perturbation strength removes a per-gene state layer by construction -- drop that one match and the same pairs give 1.113x. That is the size of what the test removes, and it is why this layer is scored as a covariate rather than against the 1.208x PPI reference.
limits: one cell line and one growth condition per assay: ENCODE K562 is not the K562 the Perturb-seq screen was run in -- different laboratory, medium, passage. Cell-MATCHED here means the same immortalised line, not the same culture.
RNA is polyA-plus only, so non-polyadenylated transcripts (replication-dependent histones, many lncRNAs) are systematically under-measured and their TPM is not a level, it is a floor.
TPM is a steady-state level, not a synthesis rate: a short-lived transcript at the same TPM is being made far faster, and nothing here separates the two.

promoter accessibility is a peak CALL within +/-1000 bp of one annotated TSS. Genes with multiple TSSs are scored at one of them, and a promoter with no peak is below the pipeline's threshold, not demonstrably closed.

the ATAC signalValue is fold-enrichment against each experiment's own background and is NOT comparable across experiments; it is rank-normalised within experiment before combining, which preserves order and discards magnitude.
this layer is a STATE, not a response. It says what K562 looks like unperturbed; it says nothing about how expression or accessibility MOVE after a perturbation.

the layer is a per-gene covariate, not a link set, so the standard pair fast test cannot score it (Q5 shows the matching removes it by construction). Its value is measured as covariate quality and as its effect on an already-banked matched result.
Williams' t is applied to Spearman coefficients, which is an approximation; the bootstrap over genes is the primary statistic for every predictor contest here.

the decile match used by the standard fast test does not fully balance its own covariates at this sample size -- on the 213k PPI pairs it leaves a standardised difference of about 0.11 on gene responsiveness. That is a property of the reference test, inherited by every number compared against it here, and it is why residuals are reported as effect sizes as well as p-values.

the perturbation-axis contest uses one GWPS row per perturbed gene, so it is not inflated by pseudo-replication; the gene-axis and PPI arms are not de-replicated and their p-values are correspondingly optimistic (the ratios and Spearman coefficients are not).

the eight RNA experiments span 2011-2016 and five laboratories, and their median pairwise Spearman is about 0.86: the K562 expression value used here is a median over that spread, not a single measurement, and gene-level disagreement between laboratories is real and unmodelled.

items.question: the reliability ceiling, derived from raw counts
items.verdict: THE CEILING ON REPLOGLE RPE1 IS R2 = 0.477, NOT 1. Splitting each perturbation's cells into halves -- with the 11,485 non-targeting cells split alongside them, so no control noise is shared -- the halves agree at r = 0.3129 (sd 0.0004 over 20 draws) on the per-gene robust z this project defines its edges on, which Spearman-Brown puts at reliability 0.4766 for the full-size measurement. On raw lfc with the per-gene mean removed the ceiling is 0.4457. Leaving the gene main effects in gives 0.5289, but SHUFFLING the perturbation labels reproduces 32% of that number, so it is a ceiling on a quantity a gene-responsiveness baseline already owns. A model scored on perturbation-SPECIFIC RPE1 response therefore cannot exceed R2 ~0.48 however good it is: the target is 52% noise. THIS DOES NOT RESCALE THIS PROJECT'S K562 NUMBERS -- the ladder's R2 0.0151 and the 1.208x/1.070x/1.021x matched ratios were all scored on K562, whose cells were discarded when gwps.h5ad was pseudobulked, so K562's own ceiling is unmeasured and dividing by an RPE1 one would be the cross-axis substitution this project keeps getting burned by. What it does establish is that a ceiling of this kind exists and is nowhere near 1, and that the same computation is cheap wherever cell-level counts survive. Per perturbation the profile reliability is 0.441 (33% of perturbations beat the 95th percentile of a label-shuffled control), essentially unchanged at 0.438 under batch-disjoint splits because splitting the control the same way cancels gemgroup depth. Reliability tracks EXPRESSION cleanly (half-r 0.145 at 9.3 CPM to 0.681 at 766 CPM, Spearman 0.776) but NOT cells-per-perturbation (-0.112): the SE falls with cells exactly as power predicts (-0.979) while the true signal falls with it just as fast (-0.340), because CRISPRi depletes the cells of perturbations that hurt. So the magnitude-vs-power confound this project found (+0.0881) is real but is NOT fixed by matching on cell count -- that matches on effect size at the same time. The median perturbation's observed rms |lfc| is 66% noise variance, and a log fold change carries a median rms SE of 0.315, 1.1x the Poisson delta-method value (1.3x for the highest-expression decile), reproduced by a cell-level bootstrap at r 0.925. Finally, the |z|>=5 cut that defines this project's 537,376-edge layer replicates its SIGN 68.9% of the time between two halves of the SAME cell line -- a LOWER bound, since both sides are half-power. That is the honest reference for the 67.2% this project measured for K562 edges evaluated on RPE1: the cross-cell-line penalty is small next to the measurement-noise penalty, because most of the loss is already there when the SAME cells are split in two. And replication PEAKS at |z|>=3 (74.0%) and falls to 68.9% at |z|>=5, on genes whose own reliability drops from 0.319 to 0.254 while their expression barely moves -- the extreme tail of a MAD-normalised z is enriched for low-reliability genes, so that threshold buys noise along with effect size.
limits: RPE1 ONLY. Split-half needs cells, and this project's K562 arm (gwps.h5ad) is already pseudobulked to 11,258 x 8,248 with the cells discarded. No ceiling is computed for K562 here, and the RPE1 ceiling must NOT be used to rescale a K562 score -- cells per perturbation, control size and library depth all differ

the random split shares gemgroups between halves so batch effects cancel and are not counted as noise; the batch-disjoint split counts them. A within-batch question takes the random number, a cross-batch question the batch number. Here they barely differ, because the control is split the same way and a depth shift cancels in the difference

Spearman-Brown assumes the halves are parallel measurements differing only in length. That holds for the random split (balanced within perturbation); for the batch split the halves are only approximately equal in size, so SB is approximate there

reliability is a property of a QUANTITY, not of a dataset. The pooled raw-lfc ceiling is largely reproduced by shuffled perturbation labels because it contains per-gene main effects; only the gene-mean-removed and robust-z ceilings bound a model scored above a responsiveness baseline

the empirical SE captures cell sampling and cell-to-cell biological variability. It does NOT capture guide-level effects (off-target activity, variable knockdown), which are shared by every cell carrying that guide and therefore cancel in a within-perturbation split -- so every reliability here is an OVER-estimate with respect to 'what does losing this gene do'

cells-per-perturbation is not a clean power axis: CRISPRi depletes cells carrying guides against genes whose loss is costly, so low-cell perturbations have systematically LARGER true effects. Noise and signal both fall as cells rise and reliability stays roughly flat
perturbations below 25 cells (271 of 2394) are outside the analysis set; their reliability is not reported

8,749 genes are measured. A gene not measured has no reliability here and absence is unknown rather than zero; dropout is reported per gene so the missingness is visible, and it is strongly expression-dependent

the R2 ceiling assumes observed = signal + independent noise. Noise correlated between the halves (ambient RNA, index hopping, a systematic artefact shared by a perturbation's cells) would be counted as signal and would push the true ceiling LOWER

the edge-replication rows select on a HALF-sized measurement and evaluate on the other half, so both sides are noisier than a full-data measurement. Those agreement rates are a LOWER bound on full-power within-dataset replication

`noise_fraction` and `1 - reliability` are NOT the same number and must not be quoted interchangeably. noise_fraction is SE^2 / rms(lfc)^2, taken about zero, so a perturbation's mean shift across genes counts as signal; reliability is a CORRELATION, so each profile is mean-removed first and only gene-to-gene structure counts. The first answers 'how much of the measured magnitude is noise', the second 'how much of the measured pattern is reproducible', and they can differ severalfold for one perturbation

items.question: does the dynamics null replicate on time- and dose-resolved data?
items.verdict: THE NULL DOES NOT REPLICATE: THE EARLY PROFILE CARRIES GENE-SPECIFIC INFORMATION IN 9 OF 9 ARMS, BUT MOST OF WHAT LOOKS LIKE DYNAMICS IS ONE SCALAR TIMES A CONSTANT PER-GENE VECTOR. In K562, 4 h -> 24 h (546 compound x dose pairs, 91 compounds, 978 measured landmarks, AICHI project only, predictor and target on different plates), held-out R2 is 0.0350 for a constant per-gene vector with no perturbation identity at all; 0.1083 once that same vector is scaled by a SINGLE SCALAR read off the early profile; 0.1386 and 0.1535 once the gene-specific part of the early profile is used. So 62% of everything the early measurement buys is one number per perturbation. A source swap matched on ||z_early|| within dose (24 draws, mean |d norm| 1.940 against a norm sd of 12.473) gives L3 0.0912 +/- 0.0053, beaten by the real profile in 24/24 draws; the paired t-test on per-pair error fires on 100% of draws while the rank test fires on 8%, because only 45% of pairs improve and the gain is carried by the responsive minority. With a real three-point clock (LKCP, 6/24/48 h, one project, 2,077 complete series across 3 cell lines -- in U2OS/MCF7/A549 because K562 has no such series anywhere in LINCS), predicting the 48 h profile from the 24 h profile alone gives L3 0.4797-0.4909; from the 6 h profile alone 0.2965-0.3077; and from BOTH with their own fitted slopes 0.4839-0.4954. The earlier point adds +0.0041 to +0.0052 once the later one is in hand, in all 3 cell lines, so the response is close to Markov in the measured state: what is worth carrying is the most recent profile, not the trajectory that produced it. The census is the other half of the answer: across 1,201,944 signatures K562 has 142 perturbations, 91 at two or more times and 0 at three or more, and CMap phase 1 (473,647 signatures) has no K562 at all -- so LINCS cannot supply a K562 time course longer than two points to anyone, ever.
limits: K562 HAS NO THREE-POINT TIME COURSE IN LINCS. Its entire time axis is 4 h vs 24 h in one project (AICHI); the second K562 project (EMU, 336 signatures) is 24 h only and is excluded because including it would confound time with project. Any three-point result here is in U2OS / MCF7 / A549 and is labelled as such.
GSE92742 (CMap phase 1, 473,647 signatures, 76 cell lines) contains ZERO K562 signatures, so no amount of phase-1 data would improve the K562 time axis.

L1000 measures 978 landmark genes and INFERS 11,350; every number here is landmarks only, so nothing is said about the inferred space and the inferred space cannot be used for this test without measuring the inference model instead of the biology.

In K562/AICHI qc_pass is almost perfectly confounded with time (4 h: 8/588 pass; 24 h: 569/588) and mean TAS is 0.166 at 4 h against 0.223 at 24 h. The 4 h arm is the noisier one, so the forward test is attenuated; the reversed direction and the dose ladder are reported as the bracket, not as independent replicates.

Level 5 is a MODZ-weighted collapse of replicates, already differential against plate controls, so it carries no absolute expression and the L0 rung is a floor of exactly zero by construction rather than an estimate.

trt_cp only. Compounds are not registry entities -- BRD ids have no namespace in the registry -- so the perturbation axis of this layer is joined by nothing and is stored as an opaque key. Only the gene axis is registry-joined.
Doses are nominal treatment concentrations, not intracellular exposure; a 'dose ladder' is a ladder in what was added to the well.
Signature selection among replicate plates is the first sig_id alphabetically, which is deterministic and outcome-independent but discards real replicate information.

The two controls fail in opposite directions and neither alone is sufficient. The 24-draw source swap is matched on ||z_early|| to within ~8-15% of its sd but leaves plate POSITION free; the same-well control fixes position exactly but leaves the norm free (mean |d norm| 8.5-21 against sds of 12-27), so it is a position control and NOT a magnitude control. The claim rests on both, not on either.

A negative stratified R2 on the weak-response stratum is not a bug: within that stratum the total sum of squares is taken about the stratum's own mean, and a constant per-gene vector fitted on all compounds is actively worse than predicting nothing for a compound that did not respond. It is the honest statement that the consensus profile misleads on non-responders.

The K562 dose ladder compares two wells of the SAME detection plate (100% shared plate), while the time arms compare different plates (0% shared). The dose arm therefore carries a plate-artifact risk the time arms do not, and its larger effect should not be read as a cleaner result.

Compound identity is not deduplicated across pert_ids: the same molecule under two BRD ids would appear as two compounds and could place chemically identical material on both sides of a held-out split. Compounds are held out by pert_id, not by structure.

items.question: does kcat x [E] beat a binary required-catalyst flag?
items.verdict: KCAT BOUGHT NOTHING; THE HALF OF CAPACITY THAT WORKS NEEDS NO KCAT AT ALL. Head to head on 904 identical genes (226 required catalysts with a known kcat x [E] plus 678 required for nothing; 344 required genes DROPPED rather than scored as zero because their kcat is unknown), the binary flag scores Spearman +0.0388 / AUC 0.5181 and the continuous capacity burden +0.0415 / AUC 0.5201 -- raw held-out values, never a difference from a shuffle. Capacity does not separate them. Inside the required-catalyst class, where the flag is constant and can say nothing, low kcat x [E] genes carry dep_frac 0.1888 against 0.1519 for high-capacity genes matched on PPI degree, reaction count and K562 abundance (+0.0369, 0% of 25 draws p<0.05, 166 genes/draw, residual imbalance clean at p>=0.71): not detectable. But that arm's smallest detectable difference at 80% power is 0.133, against the +0.081 the binary flag itself achieved -- so this is a well-controlled arm that could not have found the reference effect, and it is a CEILING ON WHAT WAS TESTED rather than evidence that capacity is uninformative. The arms separate what is doing the work. Abundance-only [E] is NOT a usable arm: its capacity correlates with the matching variable at Spearman +0.86, so it splits on very nearly the quantity it is matched on, the abundance residual comes back at p 3e-07, and its +0.0097 is reported as a failed match rather than a null. kcat alone -- the number that was supposed to be the new information -- gives +0.0902 (32% of draws, not detectable). What DOES work inside the required-catalyst class is the OTHER half of capacity -- route redundancy, how many alternative reactions produce the same non-hub metabolite -- and it is computed from stoichiometry alone, with no kcat and no proteomics. Genes whose required reactions have the fewest alternative producers carry dep_frac 0.3207 against 0.2101 (+0.1106, 76% of 25 draws p<0.05, 278 genes/draw), matched on PPI degree x reactions x abundance x required-count x publications. Its raw core match FAILED on reaction count (p 0.0002) and required-count (p 4e-05), so the core +0.1558 is discarded and the number quoted is the strictest CLEANLY matched level. It is not the acyl-chain bookkeeping artefact that killed the binary flag at 3+ reactions: the low-redundancy class is 16% fatty acid oxidation against 2%, but dropping each top subsystem in turn leaves the effect at +0.1147 to +0.1195, including +0.1187 at 100% of draws with fatty acid oxidation removed entirely. kcat is unknown for 57% of catalysed reactions and is stored as None, never 1.0, so the kcat arms run on the characterised 43% and the binding constraint is coverage, not method: only 226 of 996 required catalysts have both a kcat and a K562 protein measurement, and the K562 proteome covers a set with mean dep_frac 0.271 against 0.027 for the genes it misses (p 1e-45), so absence is unknown and strongly non-random.
limits: kcat is UNKNOWN for 4,448/7,782 (57%) of catalysed reactions and is stored as None, never 1.0; capacity is therefore undefined -- not low -- for that majority, and every kcat arm below runs on the characterised minority

kcat coverage is not missing at random: it tracks how well-studied an enzyme is, and the coverage table reports the dep_frac of covered vs uncovered genes so the direction of that bias is visible rather than assumed

the GENE tier is a kcat for the enzyme, but still not for THIS cell: SABIO-RK values are in vitro, at assorted pH and temperature, on purified protein, and in vivo apparent kcat is typically well below them

capacity here is kcat x [E] -- an in-vitro CEILING. It contains no substrate concentration, no saturation, no allosteric or PTM regulation and no flux, so a reaction can sit orders of magnitude below this ceiling; the project's own kapp module found the median reaction ~30 orders below its ceiling under FBA

Human-GEM is a generic human model, so a reaction present here may be inactive in K562, while the abundance and the K562 gene effect are cell-specific -- the layer mixes one generic axis with two cell-specific ones and only the latter two are pinned to a cell

36% of the proteome is measured in the K562 iBAQ layer and coverage is steeply abundance-dependent, so [E] is a lower bound wherever an OR branch is unmeasured (flagged `E_*_complete`) and undefined wherever an AND subunit is
dep_frac is a pan-cancer summary and the K562 gene effect is one line; neither is a metabolic flux measurement, so this tests transfer between layers, not against a metabolic gold standard

route_alternatives counts reactions sharing a non-hub product (hub cutoff 50 producing reactions) -- a topological proxy for redundancy, not a proven bypass: a counted alternative may be in the wrong compartment, unexpressed in K562, or thermodynamically infeasible, and no flux calculation was run to check that any of them can actually carry the load. It is also the arm that survived, so it carries the most weight and the least mechanism

the surviving route-redundancy effect is measured on a HUB CUTOFF chosen a priori at 50 producing reactions and not swept; a different currency-metabolite definition would give a different alternatives count

the kcat arms are not merely null, they are underpowered: at 152-174 matched genes per draw the smallest detectable difference at 80% power is 0.11-0.16 dep_frac, above the +0.081 the binary flag itself achieved, so they bound what was tested rather than showing kcat is uninformative

items.question: how much of the K562 regulatory landscape can the E-G layer even reach?
items.verdict: (no verdict field; reports module, source, assembly, provenance_asserted)
limits: ENCODE Registry V3 only. V4 (2.35M cCREs, different class vocabulary) is NOT merged; mixing the two would put two annotation versions on one axis.

K562 classification comes from ONE file, ENCFF210CAN (zhiping-weng:cCREs-GRCh38-V6-EFO_0002067-ENCSR000EOT-7group). Five of the six V3 K562 annotations on the ENCODE portal are DNase-only and classify 0 elements as enhancers; this module asserts 100% All-data/Full-classification and would raise on any of them.

the cCRE class is a QUALITATIVE call (PLS/pELS/dELS/CTCF-only/DNase-only/Low-DNase). No accessibility z-score is carried, because the portal's bed9+ cell-type files do not contain one. 'K562-accessible' is therefore a threshold someone else chose, not a continuous covariate this module can re-tune.

gene coordinates come from the registry's 16,380 genes with a TSS, which is the cell object's gene set. cCREs whose only nearby gene is outside that set are counted as unreachable, which is true of the model but not of the genome.
one TSS per gene. Alternative promoters would move some distances across the 100 kb / 250 kb boundaries the census turns on; the direction of that bias is toward UNDER-stating reachability.
the E-G geometry (250 kb window, empty 100-250 kb stratum) is read from outputs/orphan/eg_layer.json, not recomputed; if that layer is retrained the census must be rerun.

the benchmark K562 arm is EIGHT screens (Gasperini2019, Nasser2021, Schraivogel2020, K562_DC_TAP, Xie, Morris, Klann, Reilly) with different libraries and hit rates. Dataset is a matching stratum in test 4 for exactly that reason; the pooled positive rate across them is not a property of K562.

absence of a cCRE call is UNKNOWN, not 'not an element': SCREEN's universe is itself derived from DNase peaks, so an element with no DNase in any biosample was never registered and is invisible here as well as to the E-G layer.
no edge is scored or emitted. This module delivers a candidate universe and a census; it does not claim any element regulates any gene.

the 95.7% recall of validated positives by K562-accessible cCREs is measured ONLY among elements the benchmark chose to test, and those screens preferentially targeted accessible chromatin. Genome-wide recall is therefore at most this and probably lower; it cannot be estimated from a benchmark that shares the selection criterion.

the matched test reuses controls (10,467 treated vs a 1,573-pair control pool), so the Fisher p on the full draw is optimistic. A balanced without-replacement variant is reported alongside it and is the one to read for significance.

'Significant' is the benchmark's own call at its own FDR, and power differs by screen. Pairs below PowerAtEffectSize25 0.8 are excluded rather than counted as negatives, because not-detected is not not-linked.
the (cCRE, gene) pair count is compared to the E-G layer's peak-derived candidate count as a SIZE comparison only; the K562 accessibility peak file is not on disk, so their overlap is unmeasured.

items.question: translation efficiency as the missing mRNA->protein multiplier
items.verdict: ENCODE HAS NO RIBOSOME PROFILING -- not for K562, not for any biosample: the assay_title facet was read live and carries 67 titles, none of them ribosome-profiling. The direct measurement of translation efficiency is unavailable from this source, so what follows is a steady-state protein-per-mRNA ratio and is not the same quantity. That ratio spans 1.4 log10 (24x) across 5,857 genes, which looks like a multiplier worth having -- and it is not one. It correlates -0.875 with log mRNA and +0.092 with log protein: log mRNA varies 2.1x more than log iBAQ protein here, so the difference of the two logs inherits the denominator and the quantity is 77% inverse expression. Its bottom decile holds 69 ribosomal proteins against 2 in the top -- it is sorting genes by how much mRNA they have. AN EMPIRICAL PROTEIN-PER-mRNA RATIO IS THEREFORE NOT A USABLE STAND-IN FOR TRANSLATION EFFICIENCY, and that is the single most important thing this module establishes. It IS predictable from sequence and annotation alone: chromosome-held-out R2 0.236 (Spearman 0.401) against a shuffled-feature null of -0.046 (max -0.038 over 20 shuffles, 47 null SDs, p 0.0476). But 60% of that is LENGTH: dropping cds/transcript length and exon counts takes it to 0.094, and the strongest single correlate is log CDS length (+0.278 Spearman). iBAQ divides intensity by the number of theoretically observable peptides and short proteins are the ones mass spectrometry misses, so the length term is entangled with the assay's own normalisation and must not be read as translation biology. What survives the ablation is still real (R2 0.094 vs null max -0.032, 23 null SDs). The arm that does NOT route through the ratio is the one that survives. On the decision that matters -- predicting K562 protein level -- mRNA alone reaches held-out R2 0.167, mRNA plus sequence 0.235 (+0.068, i.e. 41% relative, against a mRNA-plus-shuffled-features null of -0.047, 42 null SDs), and sequence alone 0.075. With the length features dropped the combined arm still reaches 0.198 (+0.031 over mRNA alone), so the ceiling does move on non-length sequence features and not only on the assay artefact. On the fast test it marks no ELEVATED pairs: arm1 0.999x, arm2 0.913x, arm3 1.001x against matched controls, none of them above the ~1.05 bar that PPI (1.208x) and co-dependency (1.070x) clear. That is the result stated in advance rather than a disappointment -- the fast test scores PAIRS and this is a PER-GENE layer, whose value if any lies on the mRNA->protein axis that Perturb-seq cannot see at all. Arm2 sits at 0.913x, a depletion rather than an enrichment -- and since its 'high ratio' genes are largely low-mRNA genes, it would not have been a translation result even had it held -- but its residual imbalance (0.0027/0.17) leaves it uninterpretable rather than reversed. The binding constraint is not the model, it is the measurement: only 71% of GWPS genes have a K562 protein value and missingness is strongly expression-dependent (p 1.62e-181), so the ratio is left-censored exactly where it would be most informative.
limits: THE RATIO IS DOMINATED BY ITS DENOMINATOR. It correlates -0.87 with log mRNA and +0.09 with log protein, because log mRNA varies about twice as much as log iBAQ protein over these genes. Ranking genes by this ratio very largely ranks them by inverse expression, so it is NOT a usable translation multiplier and any analysis keyed on it inherits that. The protein-level prediction in `downstream_protein_prediction` deliberately does not route through the ratio and is the result that survives

NOT ribosome profiling. ENCODE has no Ribo-seq for K562 or for any biosample; this is a steady-state protein/mRNA ratio, which confounds translation rate with protein degradation rate and cannot separate them

two assays, two normalisations: iBAQ is a within-sample intensity divided by the number of theoretically observable peptides, Perturb-seq mean is a normalised UMI mean. Their ratio has no absolute units and is comparable only within this table

LEFT-CENSORED and the censoring is expression-dependent: the ratio exists only where mass spectrometry detected the protein, so genes with genuinely low protein per mRNA are preferentially missing and every statistic here is computed on a biased sample
the protein table joins by GENE SYMBOL, the weakest namespace in the registry; the mRNA and perturbation tables join by ENSG
restricted to the 8,248 genes GWPS measures, which are the expressed and well-detected ones, so the ratio is unknown for most of the genome
measured in unperturbed K562 -- a STATE, not a response. It says nothing about how the protein/mRNA ratio moves after a perturbation, which is what the chain's missing arrow actually requires
predicted ratios inherit the training set's censoring and are extrapolations for any gene whose protein was never detected
one cell line, one proteomics study, one growth condition

items.question: what can a ligand-receptor layer support in monoculture?
items.verdict: THE lr LAYER IS 2% ALIVE IN K562, AND THE HALF OF NICHENET A MONOCULTURE CAN TEST IS A WELL-CONTROLLED NULL. Gating the 948 pairs on both partners being present in this cell leaves 13 pairs by mRNA and 23 (2.4%) allowing K562 proteomics as a second axis -- against 43% of cell-object genes reaching the panel, and the depletion survives matching on atlas breadth (0.146 observed vs 0.495 matched for ligands, 0.169 vs 0.476 for receptors, 25 draws). 55% of pairs with atlas masks share NO cell type expressing both partners, which is the layer being intercellular rather than broken. Second: for the 56 receptors perturbed in Replogle K562 whose cognate ligand carries a NicheNet programme, those targets move at mean |robust z| 1.007 -- against 0.933 for the ligand-swap null (1.079x, win rate 0.488, 0% of 25 draws below p 0.05) and 0.824 for a strength-matched receptor swap on the identical genes (1.222x, 4% of draws). The apparent 1.26x over responsiveness-matched random genes is the NicheNet vocabulary, not the pairing: MYC is asserted for 79% of ligands and two ligands' measured target sets already overlap at Jaccard 0.26. THE NULL IS BOUNDED, NOT DECISIVE: at n=56 the smallest detectable effect is 1.14x, and complex co-membership -- real on this readout at 1.122x with 100% of draws significant at n=1,195 -- falls to 1.080x and 8% when subsampled to n=56. So this excludes a large ligand-specific downstream programme and nothing smaller. And it tests only the intracellular half of the arrow: a receptor with no ligand in the dish has nothing to transduce, so 'no effect' and 'pathway never running' are not separable in monoculture. The lr and nichenet layers remain UNVALIDATED as communication; what is now established is how little of lr is even switched on here.
limits: MONOCULTURE CANNOT VALIDATE A MULTICELLULAR LAYER. A ligand-receptor edge asserts a sender, a receiver, spatial proximity and a downstream programme. K562 Perturb-seq supplies one cell type and no space, so three of those four are untestable here by construction and nothing below should be read as validating the lr layer as an interaction.

The receptor-perturbation test checks the INTRACELLULAR HALF ONLY: whether the programme NicheNet attributes to a ligand depends on the cognate receptor's gene product. It does not check that the ligand ever reaches the receptor.

THE NULL IS UNDERPOWERED AND SAYS SO. At n=56 receptors the smallest effect detectable at 80% power is 1.14x, and the complex-co-membership positive control run through identical machinery at the same n reaches p<0.05 in only 8% of draws. Large ligand-specific effects are excluded; small ones are not.

NicheNet's ligand-specificity is weak at source: mean Jaccard 0.26 between two ligands' measured target sets, MYC asserted for 79% of ligands. The ligand-swap control therefore shares ~40% of the cognate set and attenuates any true effect by about that much.

A receptor with no ligand present has nothing to transduce, so absence of a downstream effect is as consistent with 'the pathway was never running' as with 'NicheNet is wrong'. These two are NOT separable in this design and are not separated.

ABSENCE IS UNKNOWN, NOT ZERO. The Replogle panel is 8,248 genes with a detection floor of mean 0.10, and the K562 proteome is 7,031 proteins with strongly abundance-dependent coverage; secreted ligands are under-detected by BOTH (lysate mass-spec misses secreted protein, low-expressed transcripts fall below the panel floor). The gate is therefore biased toward calling ligands absent, which makes the surviving fraction a LOWER bound.
emask covers 7,496/16,492 genes only, and its 200 atlas cell types do not include K562 or any leukaemia line; it is used for intercellularity and breadth, never as a K562 expression call.
CRISPRi knocks down rather than out; residual receptor is not measured here.
lr and nichenet were joined by gene SYMBOL, the weakest namespace in the registry, because neither layer carries an accession.
The CELLxGENE census figures are CO-EXPRESSION across cell types, not evidence of an interaction, and are pinned to one snapshot; they validate nothing.

items.question: does cell-matched protein beat generic, across lines?
items.verdict: CELL-MATCHING BUYS A SMALL, PARTLY REAL EFFECT AND THE RAW COLUMN IS THE WRONG WAY TO USE IT. ProCan-DepMapSanger downloaded and reduced: 948 cancer cell lines x 8,457 proteins, joined on UniProt ACCESSION at 99.4%. Of the five Perturb-seq lines this project holds, three are in the panel (K-562, HCT-116, Jurkat); RPE1 is non-cancer and HepG2 was not profiled, and neither was substituted. (a) The ProCan K-562 column agrees with the PaxDb/Geiger K562 iBAQ vector already in the model at Spearman 0.622 over 4,617 shared genes -- but 40 RANDOM ProCan lines agree with the same vector at 0.488 +- 0.047, so the cell-specific margin is only +0.134: protein abundance is overwhelmingly a human constant, and that ceiling governs everything below. (b) ProCan does NOT fill PaxDb's hole. Coverage of the cell object goes 37.7% (PaxDb) -> 29.8% (ProCan K-562) -> 41.8% (union), and in the two lowest generic-abundance quintiles 7.2% -> 3.3% -> 9.8%. Both sources miss the same faint proteins; ProCan-covered genes carry mean dep_frac 0.267 against 0.029 for uncovered, so absence stays UNKNOWN, never zero. (c) Raw held-out Spearman against each line's own perturbation strength: cell-matched K562 +0.118, HCT116 +0.063, Jurkat +0.044. The raw ProCan column LOSES to PaxDb iBAQ on 3/3 lines (K562 +0.157, HCT116 +0.125, Jurkat +0.070) and to the K-562 ProCan column on 1/2 non-K562 lines -- averaged DIA intensity is not built for cross-protein comparison, so that contest is a unit contest and not a matching one. With the unit confound removed by standardising each protein across the 948 lines, the purely cell-specific panel-z scores K562 +0.116 (p 2.4e-14), HCT116 +0.089 (p 1.2e-08), Jurkat +0.044 (p 0.1), positive and significant on 2/3, beating a DETECTION-MATCHED random line in K562 90%, HCT116 75%, Jurkat 75% of 40 paired draws (mean delta +0.0624), and still explaining the residual after PaxDb iBAQ is regressed out on 2/3 lines (K562 +0.081 (p 3.1e-07), HCT116 +0.068 (p 3.5e-05), Jurkat +0.038 (p 0.17)). The operational reading: carry an iBAQ-like absolute abundance for the LEVEL, and carry the pan-cancer panel-z as a SEPARATE cell-specific field -- not as a replacement column.
limits: 948 CANCER cell lines only: RPE1 (hTERT-immortalised, non-cancer) and HepG2 are absent, so two of the five Perturb-seq lines this project holds cannot be cell-matched at all and are reported as absent rather than substituted
39% of the matrix is not quantified and detection is abundance- and line-dependent; a missing entry is UNKNOWN, never zero
averaged log2 DIA intensity from one pipeline and one release -- the z-scored matrix shipped in the same archive is a different normalisation and is never mixed in here

a raw ProCan column is NOT an absolute abundance scale: DIA intensity depends on peptide ionisation efficiency, so it compares one protein ACROSS cell lines well and different proteins WITHIN a cell line badly. `abundance` should not be used where iBAQ or ppm would be; `cellspecific_panelz` is the field that carries the cell-matched information and it is dimensionless by construction
a static unperturbed proteome: it says nothing about how protein moves after a perturbation, which is still the arrow the chain is missing

the Perturb-seq screens come from three different laboratories (Replogle K562/RPE1, Xaira HCT116, Nadig Jurkat/HepG2), so every head-to-head is run WITHIN one cell line and absolute values are never compared across lines
protein is matched to a gene by taking the maximum over accessions mapping to it, which discards isoform structure
perturbation strength is a pseudobulk transcriptional readout, so a knockdown that changes protein or flux without changing mRNA scores as no response
